findings.claim: The PR changed `template_for` to `(arm, issue)` and `checkout` to `(w, arm, issue)`, and `_run_one` now calls them with the extra `issue` argument. The accept scripts that stub them with the old one- and two-argument signatures (305, 307, 330, 334, 335, 336, 340) were not updated, so they now fail. The PR edits the matching `tests/test_bench_*` stubs to `lambda a, issue=None` but leaves these scripts alone.
findings.evidence: I ran `python3 bench/policy/accept/N.py $PWD` for each script. 305 gives pass:false (base_red_is_retried false, a_red_base_is_still_recorded false). 307 raises `TypeError: fake_checkout() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given`. 330 gives pass:false. 334 gives pass:false (all four timeout checks false). 335, 336 and 340 crash with KeyError ('cmd'/'cwd'), because `run_one` returns early on the TypeError and records no command. I also ran 305, 334 and 340 on a HEAD~1 worktree, and all three pass there. I did not run 331 end to end: it calls `pb.checkout(w, arm)`, which still works because `issue` defaults to None.

findings.claim: `ReadTools._task_words` caches the recorded task words for the life of the instance, and an empty result is cached too. `ProcessAPI._read` keeps one `ReadTools` per process, and the MCP server is long-lived. So if `symbol` runs before the prompt hook has recorded anything, or a later prompt changes the task, the task-aware tie-break never sees the new words. The 12-hour age-out in `session_context.load` is only checked once. The tie-break therefore uses the first prompt's words, or none, for the whole session.
findings.evidence: Read `_task_words`: `if self._task is None: self._task = session_context.load(...)`, and `load` returns an empty `frozenset()` rather than None, so it is cached. `process_api.py:348` creates `ReadTools` once and keeps it on `self._read_tools`. I confirmed in Python that `load` returns `frozenset()` before `record` and the words after it. I did not run the MCP server.

findings.claim: Re-running `devkb init --claude-hook` without `--prompt-hook` silently removes an existing devkb UserPromptSubmit hook. `_settings` strips both owned prompt commands and only re-adds one when `prompt_hook` is truthy. A user who installed `--prompt-hook router` and later refreshes with `--claude-hook` loses the router, and the docstring does not say this.
findings.evidence: I called `init._settings(root, True, prompt_hook='router')` and wrote the result to `.claude/settings.json`. A second call, `_settings(root, True)`, returned hooks keys `['PreToolUse']` only, so UserPromptSubmit was gone.

findings.claim: Risk, not reproduced: `_mentioned_in_tests` is a plain regex over the test text for any name of four or more letters, and it also matches docstring lines and string literals. For a common name such as `write`, `record` or `resolve`, it can stamp 'Incomplete for tests' on `pack refactor` even when the unresolved mentions are unrelated. I could not reproduce this: the prebuilt graph was stale or ambiguous for the names I tried, so no 'mention it' section appeared.
findings.evidence: Read the code only. `devkb pack refactor run_suite|on_prompt|write` printed no 'mention it' section, and `refactor record` printed an ambiguity list.

findings.claim: `template_for` now calls `checkout(t, arm, issue)`, and `_run_one` calls `template_for(arm, issue)`. The accept scripts that stub these with the old arities (`lambda a:`, `fake_checkout(t, arm)`) now raise TypeError. In `_run_one` that TypeError is caught as an ordinary setup error, so the run is recorded as `error` and the scripts' black-box checks never get to run. findings.evidence: I ran each script against HEAD~1 (a worktree at /tmp/base) and against HEAD. 305, 307, 330, 334, 335, 336 and 340 all pass at HEAD~1. At HEAD 305, 330 and 334 print pass:false, 307 dies with `TypeError: fake_checkout() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given`, and 335, 336 and 340 die with `KeyError: 'cmd'` or `'cwd'`. findings.claim: `ReadTools._task_words` caches the result of `session_context.load` for the life of the object, and an empty frozenset also counts as cached. `ProcessAPI` keeps one `ReadTools` for the whole MCP server process. If `symbol` runs before the first prompt was recorded, or any time before a later prompt, the task words are never re-read. The 'task-aware tie-break' then silently does nothing for the rest of the session, and a new prompt in a long session is ignored.
findings.evidence: I created `rt = ReadTools(ProcessAPI('.'))`. `rt._task_words()` returned `frozenset()`. After `session_context.record(Path('.'), 'resolve the cpp macro expansion problem')`, `session_context.load` returned five words but `rt._task_words()` still returned `frozenset()`.

findings.claim: `_settings` always strips devkb-owned UserPromptSubmit entries and only re-adds one when `prompt_hook` is passed. Re-running `devkb init --claude-hook` without `--prompt-hook` therefore silently uninstalls a previously installed router or context hook, which breaks the 'idempotent refresh' contract. The CLI also accepts `--prompt-hook` without `--claude-hook` and ignores it with no message.
findings.evidence: With `init.run(root,'lean-pack',False,False,True,'router')`, settings.json contained UserPromptSubmit. After a second `init.run(...,True,None)` it was gone (printed `after plain rerun: False`). `run()` only calls `_settings` when `claude_hook or not install`.

findings.claim: `_mentioned_in_tests` treats any quoted occurrence of the name as a mention, and skips only lines that start with `#`. Common names in unrelated test strings (a dict key `"name"`, `"load"`, an error message), or a trailing `# foo(...)` comment, are listed as 'mentions with no call the graph resolved'. That also rewrites the Coverage verdict to **Incomplete for tests** for that function.
findings.evidence: Read from the regex `[\"']{n}[\"']` and the line filter in `packs.py`, and the `cov = ... Incomplete for tests` override at about line 599. I did not run a false-positive case.

findings.claim: The PR changes `_run_one` to call `template_for(arm, issue)` and `checkout(t, arm, issue)`, but the accept scripts still stub them with one- or two-argument signatures (`lambda a:`, `fake_checkout(t, arm)`). findings.claim: `ReadTools._task_words` caches the recorded task for the lifetime of the instance, and an empty set counts as cached because it is not None. In the long-lived MCP server, a prompt that arrives after the first `symbol` call (or one made before any prompt was recorded) never changes the tie-break. The 12-hour `MAX_AGE` check also never runs again after the first load.
findings.evidence: Read devkb/read_tools.py:103-107. `self._task` is set once from `session_context.load` and is never invalidated. `load` returns `frozenset()` when the file is absent, and that value is cached too.

findings.claim: Re-running `devkb init --claude-hook` without `--prompt-hook` silently removes a UserPromptSubmit hook installed earlier. The loop strips the owned prompt commands and only re-adds one when `prompt_hook` is set. A routine refresh of the block therefore turns the opt-in off. `--prompt-hook` without `--claude-hook` is also silently ignored, because `_settings` is only called when `claude_hook` or removing.

findings.claim: `_mentioned_in_tests` also matches `def name(` and local helpers of the same name in test files, and a quoted name inside a docstring. Any such hit rewrites the Coverage verdict to 'Incomplete for tests' for common names, and the comment filter only covers whole-line comments. That is noisy and could erode trust in the real signal.
findings.evidence: I read the regex `(?<![\w.])name\s*\(`. It matches a `def name(` line, which the graph already resolves. It was not exercised on a crafted case (I tried a few `devkb pack refactor` runs on this repo, none triggered the section).

findings.claim: `template_for` now passes `issue` to `checkout`, and the PR did not update the accept scripts under bench/policy/accept/ that stub them. `307.py` stubs `checkout(t, arm)`, and `305.py`, `330.py`, `334.py`, `335.py`, `336.py` and `340.py` stub `template_for = lambda a: ...`. findings.claim: `_task_words()` caches the recorded task in `self._task` for the lifetime of the `ReadTools`. `ProcessAPI` builds one `ReadTools` per process, so a long-lived MCP server reads `session-context.json` once and never sees a later prompt's words. The feature only works for a short-lived process, or for the first prompt if it was recorded before the first `symbol` call. The hook rewrites the file on every prompt, and the 12-hour expiry is never re-checked in a server that stays up.
findings.evidence: In a fixture with `resolve` defined in `a/other.py` and `b/cpp_resolve.py`, a `ProcessAPI` that had already ranked once, with no task recorded, still returned `a/other.py` first after `session_context.record(project, 'fix the cpp resolve macro bug')`. A fresh `ProcessAPI` returned `b/cpp_resolve.py` first.

findings.claim: The `_mentioned_in_tests` regex matches any `.name(` call on any receiver, and any quoted `"name"`. Common names such as `load` or `get` therefore flag unrelated test files, and the Coverage line is overridden to 'Incomplete for tests'. The Coverage text then reads '**Incomplete for tests: ...** **Complete.** ...', which contradicts itself. A false positive from `json.load(...)` or a dict key sends the agent to grep, which is the behaviour the pack exists to prevent.
findings.evidence: In a fixture where `tests/test_other.py` only uses `json.load(open('x'))` and `{"load": 1}`, `pack refactor load` listed it under 'mention it with no call the graph resolved'. The Coverage section printed both 'Incomplete for tests: 1 test file(s)...' and '**Complete.**'.

findings.claim: The UserPromptSubmit entry is always stripped when `install` is true, and only re-added if `prompt_hook` is passed. Re-running `devkb init --claude-hook` without `--prompt-hook`, the normal idempotent refresh, silently removes a previously opted-in prompt hook. It also removes one the user added by hand if its command contains `devkb hook prompt` or `devkb hook context`.
findings.evidence: `init.run(root, 'lean-pack', False, False, True, 'router')` gave hooks ['PreToolUse','UserPromptSubmit']. Re-running with `prompt_hook=None` gave ['PreToolUse'].

findings.claim: `record_task` writes the prompt words even when `DEVKB_ROUTER=0`. It also records the words of an invalid event, because `main_context` and `on_prompt` resolve the project from cwd. The record is only read by `symbol`, so the effect is limited to a wrong tie-break, and only if the hook runs from a subdirectory with its own `.devkb`.
findings.evidence: Read from router.py:339-340 and 359-363. Not run.

findings.claim: `template_for(arm, issue)` and `checkout(w, arm, issue)` changed signature, but the accept scripts stub them with the old arity (`lambda arm: ...`, `fake_checkout(t, arm)`). `bench/policy/accept/305.py`, `307.py`, `330.py`, `334.py`, `335.py`, `336.py` and `340.py` now fail, so the acceptance checks for those tickets no longer pass.

At HEAD: 307 raises `TypeError: fake_checkout() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given`; 305 prints pass:false (`base_red_is_retried` false); 330 and 334 print pass:false; 335, 336 and 340 raise `KeyError: 'cmd'`/`'cwd'` because the stub raises before the code under test runs. The prompt hook writes a new record on every prompt, but a long-lived MCP server never rereads it. The task-aware tie-break therefore uses the first record seen, or none, for the whole session.
findings.evidence: I built a two-file fixture with `resolve` defined in `a/cpp_resolve.py` and `a/other.py`, then used one `ProcessAPI` instance. `symbol resolve` returned `a/other.py::resolve` first. I called `session_context.record(...)` with 'fix cpp_resolve macro bug' and queried again on the same instance: still `a/other.py::resolve`. `tests/test_task_ranking.py` only runs a fresh CLI process per query, so it never covers this.

findings.claim: `_mentioned_in_tests` flags any test that calls the name, even when the graph resolved that call to a different same-named definition. The pack then says the list is incomplete, and the Coverage line also says Complete.
findings.evidence: I built a fixture with `compute_total` defined in `pkg/a.py` and `pkg/b.py`, plus `tests/test_a.py` calling a's and `tests/test_b.py` calling b's, both resolved by the graph. `pack refactor pkg/a.py::compute_total` listed `tests/test_b.py:3` under 'mention it with no call the graph resolved'. Coverage read `**Incomplete for tests: 1 test file(s) mention ...** **Complete.** Every call site ... was attributed`. Common method names such as `write` or `update` will behave the same way, since the regex also matches any `.name(`.

findings.claim: `compare_arms` counts a cut-off run's unknown cost (`None`) as $0.00. That biases the mean down and the interval for the cost difference, contradicting the #303 rule that `summary` follows (a cut-off cost is unknown, not zero).
findings.evidence: Read at line 201: `"cost $": lambda x: x["cost"] if x["cost"] is not None else 0.0`. `summary()` at line 119 drops the `None` values. The existing `table()` therefore leaves cut-off runs' cost out of its means while `--compare` includes them as zeros.

findings.claim: The `TICKET` regex treats any `#<1-6 digits>` as a ticket id. A hex colour or similar in a prompt routes it as a ticket pack lookup, and the ticket route takes precedence over `navigate`.
findings.evidence: `router.classify('make the button color #000000 darker in theme.css please')` returned `Route(name='ticket', subjects=['000000'])`. `classify('see C# 12 and issue #7 in the notes')` routed to ticket 7, which is intended. With the router opt-in, the cost of a mistaken route is a wasted `pack ticket` call and a log row.

findings.claim: `error_bundle` takes `re.match(...).group(1)` of the first kept raiser line without a None check. A line shaped differently from `- \`file::name\`` raises AttributeError. `main` swallows it, but then the decision is never logged and the prompt gets no bundle.
findings.evidence: Read of lines 193-212: `proven_raisers` matches `- \`([^\`:]+)::` but `error_bundle` uses the different pattern `- \`[^\`]*::([^\`]+)\``, and the unguarded `.group(1)` runs inside `main`'s catch-all. I did not construct a failing pack, so this is from reading only.

findings.claim: `nav_habits.py` and `replay_queries.py` crash with ZeroDivisionError or ValueError on an empty selection. `nav_habits.py` divides by `tot` (the grep count) with no guard. `replay_queries.table` calls `max()` over an empty `by_dist` when there are no symbol queries. `base_graph` raises StopIteration or IndexError when no run checkout or commit exists.
findings.evidence: Read only: `100 * v / tot` over `greps.most_common()` is skipped when empty, but `tot` is used in the header and shares; `max(len(x) for x in by_dist.values())` in replay_queries.table has no empty guard; `next(p for p in sorted([...]))` has no default.

findings.claim: `_run_one` now calls `template_for(arm, issue)` and `checkout(w, arm, issue)` with two or three arguments. The `bench/policy/accept/*.py` scripts, which the PR did not edit, still stub them with one or two. Six of the eight accept scripts I ran now fail.
findings.evidence: I ran `python bench/policy/accept/<n>.py <repo>`. Results: 305 `pass:false`, 330 `pass:false`, 334 `pass:false`; 335, 336 and 340 raised `KeyError` on `got['cmd']` or `got['cwd']` because the stubbed `template_for` raised `TypeError`; 307 raised `TypeError: fake_checkout() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given`; 331 still passed. The PR updated only the matching pytest files (`lambda a, issue=None`), not the accept scripts, so the pytest suite stays green while the acceptance checks fail.

findings.claim: `_task_words` loads the recorded task once and caches it on `ReadTools` forever, including an empty result. `ProcessAPI._read()` keeps one `ReadTools` for the life of the MCP server. In the MCP server, the tie-break therefore uses the task words from the first `symbol` call, or none if no prompt had been recorded yet, and ignores every later prompt.
findings.evidence: `self._task` is set only while it is None (read_tools.py:104-109). `ProcessAPI._read` caches the object (process_api.py:345-349), and `mcp_server.py:40` creates the `ProcessAPI` once. I confirmed this by reading the code, not by running it. The `MAX_AGE` expiry is also only checked at that first load, so a stale task never ages out.

findings.claim: Re-running `devkb init --claude-hook` without `--prompt-hook` silently removes a previously installed UserPromptSubmit router or context hook. The ownership filter runs on every install and only re-adds the hook when `prompt_hook` is set. The `--remove` path also matches any user hook whose command merely contains `devkb hook prompt` or `devkb hook context` as a substring.
findings.evidence: I ran `_settings(root, True, 'router')` then `_settings(root, True, None)`. The resulting hooks keys were only `['PreToolUse']`. A user hook `my-wrapper devkb hook prompt-extra` was dropped by `_settings(root, False)`, which then returned None.

findings.claim: `_mentioned_in_tests` matches a bare `name(`, so it also matches a test file's own `def name(` and any quoted string or unrelated receiver call. Common names of four or more letters such as `build`, `run` or `parse` will therefore list unrelated test files. The Coverage line is then forced to 'Incomplete for tests', which says the opposite of what the graph resolved.
findings.evidence: The compiled regex returned True for `def build(x):`, `x = 'build'`, `assert out == "build"` and `self.build()`, and False only for comment lines. Nothing excludes a `def` line, and the match is by name only, so tests that call a different same-named symbol also count.

findings.claim: A backticked file name such as `requirements.txt` passes the `_names` filter and becomes a 'navigate' subject, because LOCATED only excludes names with `:line`. Each such name costs a graph `symbol` call, and the router makes no fuzzy-match effort to drop it.
findings.evidence: `classify('please bump dependencies in `requirements.txt` carefully')` returned `navigate` with subjects `['requirements.txt']`.

findings.claim: `_task_words()` caches the recorded task for the life of the `ProcessAPI`/`ReadTools` instance, and an empty result is cached too. In the long-lived MCP server the task-aware tie-break therefore never sees a prompt recorded after the first `symbol` call, and never ages out the 12h `MAX_AGE`. The `symbol` call before the first prompt, the common case, freezes it to 'no task' for the whole session. The CLI is unaffected because it is one process per call.
findings.evidence: Built a `ReadTools` subclass with `_task=None`. `_task_words()` returned frozenset(). After `session_context.record(d, 'fix the cpp_resolve macro bug please')` in the same process it still returned frozenset().

findings.claim: `_mentioned_in_tests` also counts a test file's own `def name(` line, and a call quoted inside a docstring or other string. The 'not in a comment' guard only skips `#` lines. A test that defines its own helper with the same name is flagged. The report points at the `def` line, and the Coverage verdict is forced to 'Incomplete for tests', which weakens the verdict.
findings.evidence: Built a repo with `tests/test_def.py` (a local `def compute_total(x)`) and `tests/test_doc.py` (a docstring saying 'calls compute_total(items)'). `pack refactor 'pkg/calc.py::compute_total'` listed `tests/test_def.py:1` and `tests/test_doc.py:2` as mentions and printed 'Incomplete for tests: 4 test file(s)...'.

findings.claim: Two `classify` routing defects. (1) The `TICKET` regex `[A-Z]{2,10}-\d{1,6}` matches ordinary tokens such as UTF-8, SHA-256 or ISO-8601. The ticket route wins over `navigate`, so the backticked name in the prompt is dropped and the router pushes nothing. (2) A prompt that names a ticket and also has a CHANGE phrase, on a branch with no diff, falls through. The ticket is dropped even though `#123` is named. (3) A line like 'Error handling: ...' matches `TRACE`/`ERROR_LINE` and routes to `error`.
findings.evidence: `classify('Please add UTF-8 handling to `parse_header` in the loader')` returned route ticket, subjects ['UTF-8']. `classify('Address the review feedback on #123 please, thanks')` returned none. `classify('Error handling: please improve how the loader reports failures')` returned error.

findings.claim: `table()` crashes with `ValueError: max() arg is an empty sequence` whenever the replayed set has no `symbol` queries, for example `REPLAY_TICKETS` pointing at a ticket whose agents only used `uses` or `pack`. The result JSON has already been written, but the table is never printed.
findings.evidence: `replay_queries.table([{'kind':'uses','ticket':'1','args':'foo','chars':3,'answered':True,'hit':True}])` raised ValueError.

findings.claim: `run()` builds `cmd` from recorded agent commands and runs it with `shell=True`. Only `;`, `&`, `|` and newline are cut off in `extract`, so `$(...)` or backticks inside a recorded devkb argument execute during replay. The replay processes untrusted agent output.
findings.evidence: Read: `QUERY` captures `([^;&|\n]*)`; `run()` does `subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, ...)`. Not executed.

findings.claim: Two `devkb init` behaviours are silent. Re-running `devkb init --claude-hook` without `--prompt-hook` removes a previously installed prompt hook. Passing `--prompt-hook` without `--claude-hook` is silently ignored, because `_settings` is only called `if claude_hook or not install`. A user who ran `--claude-hook --prompt-hook router` and later refreshes with plain `--claude-hook` loses the router with no message.
findings.evidence: Read `run()`/`_settings`. The new test `test_devkb_init.py` asserts the removal as intended, so it is a design choice, but there is no warning or output for it.

findings.claim: The script pins `devkb[mcp]>=0.2.15` but `pyproject.toml` is at 0.2.14, so `uvx` could not resolve it if the hook were registered. Also, `exec ... || exit 0` exits 127 when the command is missing, because a failed `exec` terminates the shell before `||` runs. The script is not registered in `hooks.json`, so this is currently unreachable. `pre-edit.sh` has the same exec pattern.
findings.evidence: `DEVKB_CMD=/nonexistent bash prompt.sh` gave rc=127. `grep ^version pyproject.toml` gave 0.2.14.

findings.claim: `grep_patterns` treats `--regexp=PAT` as a flag with a value and then takes the next positional (a path) as the pattern. The replay and habit statistics that use `searches_in` then count a path as a search term.
findings.evidence: Read: `t.startswith('--') and '=' in t: i += 1`, then the next non-flag token becomes `pat`. Not run.

findings.claim: `devkb_targets` for Bash takes the first non-dash token after the subcommand as the target. A flag with a value (`devkb symbol --limit 5 parse_args`, `--under src`) makes the value the target, so the real name is missed. `5` is not distinctive, so the query is dropped from the re-fetch statistics and `queries` is undercounted.
findings.evidence: Read: `args = [a for a in rest.split() if not a.startswith('-')]; raw += args[:1]`. Not run.

findings.claim: The final summary divides by `tot['runs']`. When no run in `runs/` matches the tickets, it raises ZeroDivisionError.
findings.evidence: Read: `n / r` with r = 0 when no stream matches. Not run.

findings.claim: `_task_words` caches the recorded task for the life of the ReadTools instance (`self._task is None` check, and an empty frozenset is cached too). ProcessAPI keeps one ReadTools per process, so in the long-lived MCP server a later prompt's words, or a record written after the first `symbol` call, never reach the ranking. The 12-hour age-out also never applies to an already-loaded record.
findings.evidence: Built a 3-way `resolve` project. Created `ProcessAPI`, called `symbol resolve` (project_context.py first), then `session_context.record(p, 'Fix the C++ macro ... cpp_resolve')` and called again. The order stayed project_context.py first. The new tests (test_task_ranking.py) spawn a fresh CLI per call, so they pass without exercising this.

findings.claim: `_mentioned_in_tests` matches any `.name(` or `name(` or quoted name in every test file, with no check that the receiver is the symbol. For shared or common names it lists most of the test suite and forces `Incomplete for tests` onto the Coverage verdict. That gives the reader nothing to act on and also prefixes a duplicate 'Incomplete'.
findings.evidence: On this repo, `pack refactor devkb/read_tools.py::ReadTools.resolve` gives '118 test files mention it' (it matches `Path.resolve()` etc.). `ProcessAPI.call` gives 17 files, and the Coverage reads `**Incomplete for tests: 17 ...** **Incomplete: calls under this name from 46 ...`. `Packer._name` gives Complete. The 4-letter minimum does not help with names like resolve or call.

findings.claim: The `_settings` owned-hook filter uses substring matching (`o in command`), so it deletes a user's own UserPromptSubmit hook that merely contains `devkb hook context` or `devkb hook prompt` in its command. Re-running `init --claude-hook` without `--prompt-hook` also silently removes a previously installed prompt hook, so the refresh is not idempotent.
findings.evidence: Put `{"command":"my.sh && devkb hook context-extra"}` in .claude/settings.json and ran `devkb init --no-build --claude-hook`; the entry was gone and the UserPromptSubmit key dropped. Also ran `init --claude-hook --prompt-hook router` (1 UserPromptSubmit), then `init --claude-hook` (0).

findings.claim: `--prompt-hook` is silently ignored unless `--claude-hook` is also passed: settings.json is written only `if claude_hook or not install`. There is no error and no change is reported.
findings.evidence: `devkb init --no-build --prompt-hook router` in a fresh repo created only .gitignore and .mcp.json; no .claude directory.

findings.claim: `compare_arms` turns a cut-off run's unknown cost (None) into 0.0. The table's `summary` leaves those out on purpose (#303: 'not a zero'). The new arm-vs-arm cost difference and its 90% interval are biased toward whichever arm has more cut-off runs.
findings.evidence: Read: `"cost $": lambda x: x["cost"] if x["cost"] is not None else 0.0`, against summary()'s `if x.get(k) is not None` filter. Not run.

findings.claim: `_WITH_VALUE` lacks `--exclude-dir` and `--type-add`, and long options with a separate value fall through the `--` branch as value-less flags. The next token is then taken as the search pattern, so these replay scripts (stale_replay, inline_replay, nav_habits) count the wrong pattern.
findings.evidence: `grep_patterns('grep -rn --exclude-dir node_modules foo_bar .')` returned ['node_modules']. `rg --type-add x:y -n baz src` returned ['x:y'].

findings.claim: The script's 'never fails the prompt' claim does not hold: `exec cmd || exit 0` never reaches `exit 0`, because a failed exec exits the shell with 127. The script is not registered in hooks.json, and pre-edit.sh has the same pattern.
findings.evidence: `DEVKB_CMD=/nonexistent bash prompt.sh </dev/null; echo $?` printed 127.

findings.claim: `template_for(arm, issue)` and `checkout(t, arm, issue)` are now called with an extra argument, but 7 acceptance scripts in bench/policy/accept/ still stub them with the old signature. They now fail or report pass:false, and the PR doesn't touch them. 307 raises a TypeError; 305, 330 and 334 report pass:false; 335, 336 and 340 crash with a KeyError.
findings.evidence:
Ran `python bench/policy/accept/N.py .` for each at HEAD and at HEAD~1. At HEAD~1 all of 305, 307, 330, 334, 335, 336 and 340 print pass:true. At HEAD:
- 307: `TypeError: fake_checkout() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given`.
- 305, 330, 334: pass:false.
- 335, 336, 340: `KeyError: 'cmd'` or `'cwd'`, because the stubbed `template_for = lambda a:` raises inside `run_one` and the captured value is never set.
The stubs are `lambda a:` or `lambda arm:` in accept/305.py, 330.py, 334.py, 335.py, 336.py and 340.py, plus `fake_checkout(t, arm)` in 307.py. accept/331 still passes.

findings.claim: `_task_words` caches the loaded words on the `ReadTools` instance forever, so a long-lived `ProcessAPI` (the MCP server, which keeps one `ReadTools` via `_read()`) never sees a later prompt's record. An empty result is cached too, so the 12-hour expiry never applies and the tie-break is silently absent or stale for the server's life.
findings.evidence: Built a two-definition project, created `ProcessAPI`, and called `symbol resolve` once. Then ran `session_context.record(t, 'fix the cpp resolve step please')` and called `symbol` again. The order stayed ['a/other.py::resolve', 'a/cpp_resolve.py::resolve'] on both calls. Only the CLI test, which builds a fresh instance per call, passes.

findings.claim: `_mentioned_in_tests` matches `.name(` on any receiver, a test's own `def name(`, and any call of a same-named local. For common names this puts unrelated tests in the section and flips Coverage to 'Incomplete for tests'. The result also reads 'Incomplete for tests ... **Complete.** ...' back to back.
findings.evidence: For `pkg/calc.py::items`, `tests/test_b.py` contains only `list(d.items())` (the dict method) and `tests/test_c.py` defines its own `def items`. `pack refactor 'pkg/calc.py::items'` listed both as 'mention it with no call the graph resolved (2)', and printed `**Incomplete for tests: 2 test file(s) ...** **Complete.** Every call site ...`.

findings.claim: Re-running `devkb init --claude-hook` without `--prompt-hook` removes a previously installed UserPromptSubmit devkb hook without saying so. Re-running init is meant to be idempotent, so a refresh quietly turns the opt-in off. `--prompt-hook` without `--claude-hook` is also silently ignored.
findings.evidence: Called `_settings(t, True, 'router')` and wrote the result. `_settings(t, True, None)` on that file then returned a config with only PreToolUse. `run()` only calls `_settings` when `claude_hook` or removing, so the flag does nothing alone.

findings.claim: `_grams` of a message with no letters or digits returns {''}, and `'' in body` is always true. `proven_raisers` then keeps every listed raiser, and the 'no listed raiser contains the message' refusal is bypassed. `ERROR_LINE` accepts any 6 to 200 characters after the colon, so `ValueError: ()()()()` reaches this.
findings.evidence: `router._grams('!!!!!!!!')` printed `{''}`. Read `proven_raisers`: `any(g in body for g in grams)` is true for the empty gram.

findings.claim: The TICKET regex treats any `#` followed by digits as a ticket id, including CSS colours like `#333` and anchors, so a prompt about those routes to `pack ticket` and spends a graph query.
findings.evidence: `router.classify('see #333 colour fix on the page')` returned Route(name='ticket', subjects=['333']).

findings.claim: `finished()` calls `json.loads` on `end` with no guard, so `check_collisions` raises on a truncated or empty `end` file from an interrupted run. The batch then aborts before any run. The old `_run_one` inline check had the same flaw, but it affected one run, not the whole batch.
findings.evidence: Read `finished` and `check_collisions`, which is called on every job before the pool starts. I did not run it with a corrupt file.
